$description: Tier 3 — component tokens. Resolve to semantic tokens only.

radius.$description: A button IS a control, so it follows control/radius rather than restating a rung. Value unchanged at 8px.

Use for the card surface radius. shape/12 is the rung published as "cards and panels", which is what a card is. Raised from 8px on 2026-08-18: the token had contradicted its own role, and Card (8px) and MetricCard (12px) had already drifted apart because neither bound this token.

bg.$description: BETA badge background — ad-hoc accent (#ffd323), NOT a brand or status colour. Correctly-named entry point for the beta-badge colour.

dotSize.$description: The status/unread DOT — ONE definition for the whole estate, not one per component. Bound by the Badge's dot and by Tabs' badge; when this moves, every dot moves. It is 6 and not the on-grid 8 on purpose: beside 14px label text an 8px dot reads as a bullet rather than a signal, and 6 is what Material and Carbon both publish. A literal rather than an alias because no ref/size step is 6, and inventing one would add a scale step for a single affordance — the same reasoning layout/bar/height (46) and layout/flag/width (33) already follow. Authored in Figma first; reconciled into code 2026-08-18.

dotSizeLg.$description: The dot beside 16px body text — Badge size=lg, and Tabs size=L. A dot is sized against the TYPE it annotates, not against its container, which is why this steps with the type scale and not with the control height.

accessibilityBar.$description: AccessibilityBar (UX4G/GIGW top utility bar). Component-scoped dimensions and inverse state layers that mirror the Figma master 1:1. They live in Tier 3 because they are the bar's own geometry — a 46px bar height and a 33px flag chip are not shared scale steps, and the inverse overlays only make sense on this bar's brand fill.

height.$description: Bar height. ALIASES {layout.bar.height} rather than repeating 46px — until 2026-08-18 both carried the literal independently, so moving one silently left the other behind. layout/bar/height is the published Figma name the master binds to; this is the component-scoped handle the CSS uses.

flagWidth.$description: Flag/emblem chip width. ALIASES {layout.flag.width} rather than repeating 33px — same duplicate-literal defect as `height`, fixed 2026-08-18. Height is {size.22}, making a 3:2 chip.

pillBg.$description: ACTIVE state layer on the bar — aliases overlay/brand/active (16% white). Per the component's States documentation ACTIVE covers BOTH senses: a control being pressed, AND the current selection (the middle A at default size). One value, two meanings, deliberately — the name still says `pill` for historical reasons and is flagged for a rename.

hoverBg.$description: HOVER state layer for the bar's controls on the brand fill — aliases overlay/brand/hover (8% white). RECONCILED 2026-08-19: this branch re-created the wash at 12% from a base that predated 33cbb4f, which had already corrected 12% to 8% against the published Figma variable and the component's States documentation. 8% stands; the alias replaces the literal so the value now lives in exactly one place.

stepSize.$description: A- / A+ step button hit area.

iconButtonSize.$description: The icon button's box. Authored in Figma first, on 2026-08-18, because the exporter was silently dropping this component and .sa-abar__icbtn was drawn at a hardcoded 28px. Reconciled into code the same day.

divider.$description: The Divider component. Only the THICKNESS is component-scoped; the tones bind straight to border/neutral/*, because a rule's colour is a shared semantic — that reasoning is the designer's, from the hand-made Figma variable this replaces.

width.$description: Divider thickness — the hairline. Bound to the component's WIDTH or HEIGHT depending on orientation, not to a stroke, which is why it needs a WIDTH_HEIGHT scope that control/border/width does not carry.
